items.title: Buckingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2019
items.q: Caroline, my wife, hears this all the time about the bar keeps getting lower and lower and lower.

ctx.x: Good question. Well if you look at the greats, the legends, they certainly didn’t come from affluent background. Louis Armstrong certainly didn’t. Hank Williams certainly didn’t. I think you go to any great legendary musician and it usually comes — I mean Dolly, very humble backgrounds. You’re talking about I mean really humble backgrounds, and a lot of these people, whether it’s country, blues, jazz, rock & roll, Elvis certainly didn’t come from an affluent background. He was influenced by Chuck Berry and Fats…

least this is the way it used to be. Now, somebody told me today, one of the students said something to me about — I was talking about the recording and how it used to be, the studios. A student said, “Yeah but it might be more democratized now because everybody can make a record.” And I said, “You’re right. Everybody who has a laptop can put on garage band and make a record. But — it is democratized, but I said, “To me, to my ears, in my experience, it sounds like somebody sitting down with their computer making…
Is it true that the majority of the pop icons never went to music school? They were self- taught musicians who learned either with mentors or just through doing it.
